newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nisshin Steel sees 98/99 spending of below Y30 bln.
newsitem.headline: Nisshin Steel sees 98/99 spending of below Y30 bln.

text.p: Nisshin Steel Co Ltd said on Tuesday that it plans capital investment of less than 30 billion yen in the fiscal year starting in April 1998, and of more than 40 billion yen in 1999/2000.

The increase in 1999/2000 capital investment reflects the steelmaker's plans to replace an existing pickling facility in Sakai with a new 40-billion yen facility in Toyo, Ehime prefecture, western Japan, said Setsuo Yasuoka, a company director.
Most of the spending on the Toyo plant will take place in fiscal 1999/2000.
The company said it plans capital investment of 25 billion yen in 1997/98, which will be used mostly for rationalisation and energy conservation.
Yasuoka said spending in 1996/97 was estimated at 21 billion yen.
